To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cd2+ inhibits the ATPase and helix-destabilizing activities of BLM via a mechanism involving the binding to solvent-exposed cystein residues and the formation of large multimers/aggregats.
Cd2+ inhibits the Bloom protein via a mechanism involving binding to sulfhydril groups and formation of large protein aggregates, and that this effect is reversible upon addition of chelators.
Cd2+ inhibits the DNA repair protein BLM by binding to cysteine residues, leading to the formation of inactive multimer/aggregates and to the inhibition of DNA-binding and DNA unwinding activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism behind the inactivation of the DNA-repair protein BLM by the toxic metal Cd2+.
the mechanism of cadmium toxicity and the role of DNA repair proteins in the cellular response to cadmium.
the mechanism of Cd2+-induced inhibition of DNA-repair proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cd2+ inhibits BLM by binding to the SH groups of Cys residues and forming large aggregates of BLM, which is reversible by EDTA, but the DNA unwinding is not reversible.
Cd2+ is a potent inhibitor of BLM activity by targeting the protein's DNA binding activity and by promoting the formation of large multimers/aggregations.
cadmium inactivates BLM by multiple mechanisms including zinc substitution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd2+ inactivates BLM via multiple mechanisms including zinc substitution and direct inhibition of the DNA-binding and DNA unwinding activities.
the Cd2+-inactivation of BLM occurs via a mechanism different from those described for other zinc-containing DNA repair proteins.
Cd2+ inhibits BLM activity by targeting cysteine residues of the protein and by inducing the formation of inactive multimeric species, which are both Zn2+- and EDTA-sensitive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cd2+-induced BLM multimerization/aggregation is a major mechanism of inhibition of its DNA-unwinding activity.

BLM is inactivated by Cd2+ in a mechanism different from that of other zinc-containing repair proteins, and this inactivation occurs through two distinct mechanisms, one involving the formation of large aggregates and the other the inhibition of the ATPase and DNA-binding activities.
Cd2+-induced inactivation of BLOM may occur through multiple pathways, which are not fully understood yet.
